extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for chart question answering covering 9,608 human-written questions and 23,111 questions generated from human-written chart summaries, based on 20,882 real-world charts from four online sources. The benchmark focuses on complex visual and logical reasoning questions involving arithmetic and logical operations over charts.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different online sources: Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data (OWID), and OECD. For Pew, only chart images were crawled. For the other three, underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted. Bounding box information of chart elements was extracted from SVG files. QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk and generated from Statista human-written summaries.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Chart images, underlying data tables, metadata (e.g., title, chart type), SVG files, and associated text descriptions from Statista, Pew Research, OWID, and OECD. Topics include economy, politics, industry, social and economic issues, demographic trends, global issues, and policymaking.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were asked to provide two types of questions (compositional and visual) for each chart image, along with answers. The same questions were then answered by another annotator. If both workers' answers exactly matched, the answer was considered correct; otherwise, answers were manually checked to select the final correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowdworkers based on exact matches was 61.04%. Manual check on 500 random samples found agreement to be 78.55% when considering typos and lexical variations.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 annotations per item (one worker provides questions and answers, another worker answers the same questions)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: QA pairs were also generated from Statista human-written summaries (dataset augmentation)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a topic distribution skewed toward certain sources, with politics being particularly dominant in the Pew dataset (nearly half of charts about U.S. Politics & Policy at 45.4%). Bar charts are overrepresented compared to other chart types.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The machine-generated questions may be incomplete or not answerable from the chart due to domain mismatch in training. OCR errors can affect model performance. The benchmark only covers bar, line, and pie charts. Human annotation agreement based on exact match was only 61.04%, though higher (78.55%) when accounting for typos and lexical variations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, validation, and testing of Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) systems that involve visual and logical reasoning over real-world charts. It supports benchmarking of transformer-based QA models combining visual features and data tables.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Charts were crawled from four sources (Statista, Pew Research, OWID, OECD). Underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and text descriptions were extracted. Bounding box information of chart elements was extracted from SVG files. For data extraction, ChartOCR was adapted using key-point detection networks to locate chart elements, CRAFT model to recognize texts, and positional/color information to associate data values with text labels to produce fully-structured data tables.
